To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) DNA vaccines are a promising approach for the rapid production of vaccines for use in pandemic influenza; (2) the use of DNA vaccines in the field will require further development to improve the immunogenicity of the vaccines; and (3) DNA vaccines are an attractive approach to the rapid development of vaccines for use against emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases, including pandemic influenza.

(1) plasmid DNA vaccines have been shown to be safe and effective in human clinical trials; (2) plasmid DNAs are easy to produce and can be produced in large quantities at low cost; and (3) plasmid-based vaccines are amenable to rapid production, and the technology has been validated by a successful clinical trial of a plasmid DNA vaccine against the pandemic H1N1 influenza virus

the plasmid DNA vaccine candidate, pVAX1-NS2, is able to induce a protective immune response in the lungs against influenza H7N9 virus infection in mice, and that the immune response is mediated by both humoral and cell-mediated immune mechanisms.
